articles.title: From Bentley Pauncefoot to Yetts O’Muckhart, I’m obsessed with Britain’s weirdly named villages | Adrian Chiles
articles.summary: I was stuck in traffic when a road sign set me dreaming. If the places on it were people, what would they be like? Could Leigh Delamere be anything but the glamorous heiress to a biscuit-making fortune?
body: Stuck in traffic in the Wiltshire town of Chippenham, I chanced upon a road sign to Christian Malford and Sutton Benger. Placenames that could be people are dotted across our green and pleasant land – it’s charmingly British, somehow. Waiting to escape Friday night rush hour, I found a persona for Christian Malford taking shape. I had him down as a child actor in one of the early Harry Potters. Sutton Benger was more of a stretch, but I settled on a precociously talented young footballer of Anglo-Norwegian heritage. He signed for Chelsea with great fanfare, but never really made the grade. Poor chap.
The traffic moved on, but my mind didn’t. Once on the M4, I was soon passing Leigh Delamere, the glamorous heiress of an American biscuit-making fortune, now fallen on hard times.

Back home, I dug out my late dad’s AA road atlas of Britain (2019 edition). How I loved scouring the index in search of more imaginary friends peopling our placenames. Fun for a feeble mind? Probably. Deeply satisfying? Certainly.

articles.title: Our editors’ favorite nonstick, nontoxic pan is now at one of the steepest discounts we’ve seen
articles.summary: Our Place’s ultra-durable titanium pans can handle 1,000F heat and the dishwasher. They’re currently 30% off for Prime Day. The best Prime Day deals – and sales on home essentials. Are you trying to cut down on Pfas forever chemicals and microplastics in your kitchen?
body: This is an even better discount than Prime Day back in June, when the pan was only 10% off.

To figure out the winner, our partners at the Drexel Food Lab spent two weeks in a commercial kitchen testing 13 pans made without Pfas, PFOA, BPA and PTFE. They evaluated each for heat rate, heat retention and nonstick performance across a range of cooking and baking tasks before naming the 10.5-inch Always Pan Pro the best overall.

“The Titanium Always Pan Pro stood out for its combination of lightweight handling, impressive non-stick performance and genuinely useful design,” the research chefs at Drexel wrote. It heated evenly and eggs slid right off.

And, unlike traditional non-stick coatings that can release toxic fumes above 650F – a risk the Drexel team flagged for anyone cooking on high heat – this pan withstands up to 1000F due to its no-coating titanium construction that’s completely Pfas-free. What’s more, unlike carbon steel or cast iron (which we also love, don’t get me wrong), it requires minimal care and is safe to pop in the dishwasher.

articles.title: Model River Klein’s Personal Style Is “a Bit Messy and a Bit ’90s”
articles.summary: When she’s not modeling for Calvin Klein or Coach, River Klein’s off-duty wardrobe revolves around Hysteric Glamour tees and impeccable designer bags.
body: Gone are the days when models had to dress like a blank canvas—today’s crop of runway faces is encouraged to embrace their personal style and express their individuality through their fashion choices—be it jeans and a tee or a look-at-me statement dress. Every month, Vogue dives into the stylish wardrobes of a model of the moment to see what they’re wearing off the catwalk. Consider these the perfect references to pin to your seasonal mood board—because is there anything cooler than model-off-duty style?

This month, meet 18-year-old model River Klein. A true born-and-raised New Yorker, Klein was scouted by Heroes Model Management at just 14 years old, and she’s been booked and busy ever since. This season alone, she walked the spring 2027 shows for brands such as Coach and Ami Paris, and Klein has recently starred in campaigns for Calvin Klein and Polo Ralph Lauren, too.

Even better than her stacked resumé? Klein’s unique personal style, which she describes as “a bit messy and a bit ’90s.” Her wardrobe is stacked with vintage designer bags (Chloé Paddingtons! Fuzzy Chanels!), vintage tees, and impeccable shoes—from leather clogs to shearling boots.

articles.title: 7 US Ski Resorts That Could Benefit From El Niño This Winter
articles.summary: The 2026–27 El Niño could be the strongest on record. Before booking your next ski vacation, here's what to know.
body: The great El Niño is back, and if you’re a skier, that’s more than just a nerdy weather term—it can be the difference between a good ski trip and a great one.

The El Niño climate pattern, which is caused by warmer-than-average ocean temperatures in the tropical Pacific, can shift the winter storm track across the US. That can determine which mountains get dumped on, and which will sound like an ice-skating rink.

This year is forecasted to be a “Super” El Niño winter—meaning NOAA put the odds of a very strong El Niño as of January 2027 at 90% or greater, along with a 69% chance that the event will be the strongest on record since at least 1950. Historically, El Niño winters lead to wetter conditions in the Southern US and warmer and drier conditions in the North.

This winter's snow season is already off to an early start, with AccuWeather reporting October snowfall across the Sierra Nevada, Great Basin, and Central to Southern Rockies. According to NOAA, these initial snowfalls signal a highly active southern storm track that favors above-average precipitation for western mountain ranges like these.
points: The 2026–27 El Niño could be the strongest on record.

articles.title: Ring Designed a Keyless Smart Lock That Can Still Open When the Battery Dies
articles.summary: This past summer, I replaced the deadbolt on my front door with a smart lock, and it's possibly the best house upgrade I've ever made. I'm still not over the convenience of being able to leave the house without worrying about where my keys are, or if my absent kids have their keys.
body: Turns out that Ring built one, and the concept behind it is as simple as it is ingenious. In the first quarter of 2027, the Amazon-owned company, whose name is synonymous with video doorbells, will release its first-ever smart lock, and it will include a truly innovative feature: a built-in "Power Dial" that will allow you to manually generate enough energy to quickly unlock your door, even if the battery is totally dead—no manual key required. I got a chance to preview the mechanism at a meeting with Ring founder Jamie Siminoff, and I walked away kicking myself that I didn't wait to get one.

The Power Dial is a way to "get rid of [the need for a] backup key without the anxiety," said Siminoff, who noted that, considering the pace of technological development (he's able to turn on his Tesla using his phone), "it's insane that we still use keys [to enter our homes]"—pin tumbler locks being essentially unchanged from technology invented nearly 200 years ago. With no keyhole that can be picked, a smart lock can also be that much more secure.
